packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-18 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING

EXPOSURE / RULES STATEMENT
No proposed identification of work or author was present in my context. I read
PROMPT.md and the three image files only. I listed the packet directory (file
names and sizes) to find the images; packet.json was not opened. No web or
search tool was used.

LAYOUT SURVEY (image-only)
image-001.jpg (reduced overview): inside of a book cover (board covered in
reddish-brown leather, turn-ins visible on all sides), photographed with the
book's spine/gutter at the bottom of the frame. A white paper pastedown covers
most of the board; it is torn away at lower right and along the bottom, and
exposes underneath it a strip of parchment binding waste carrying music.
- On the paper pastedown: a printed double-ruled rectangular label, pasted on,
  with a handwritten number in ink, written sideways relative to the frame
  (reads when the image is turned 90 degrees): "3546". Reading of the digits:
  3, 5, 4, 6 - the third digit is a 4 with an open top; reasonably secure.
- Several holes and slots in the pastedown (clasp/fastening or nail positions),
  greenish staining around some (observation; cause not inferred).
- Exposed parchment waste, lower right and bottom centre: red staff lines (at
  least three, probably four, lines of one staff visible), black square/lozenge
  notation, one line of large black formal gothic text script (textualis) above
  the staff, a large red initial, and red vertical double rules at the left of
  the staff. The waste is upright with respect to the frame (text reads
  normally left to right in the image).
- At the very bottom edge of the overview, the top of the facing leaf of the
  book block is visible, upside down relative to the frame: small cursive
  script in dark ink with red rubrication/red paraph-like marks. Only a sliver
  of two or three lines is in frame; I could not read connected words from it.
  A wider view of that leaf would be needed.

Tentative interpretation (not observation): the parchment strip is a fragment
of a noted liturgical book reused as binding material. No date, origin, or
work is inferred.

SELECTED AREAS
- image-002.jpg: native-resolution tile of the lower-right exposed parchment
  (text line and staff). Overlaps the right part of the overview.
- image-003.jpg: native-resolution tile of the bottom-centre exposed parchment
  (red initial, staff start). Overlaps the overview; does not overlap
  image-002 in any legible text.
Unread: the facing leaf at the bottom edge (sliver only, upside down, too
little in frame).

TRANSCRIPTION

image-002.jpg
line 1 (text line above the staff; left end hidden under the torn paper
        pastedown, right end cut at the edge of the strip):
        [...]?tarni? si
  Letter-by-letter notes: the first surviving stroke at the tear is the right
  half of a letter (a minim or the bowl of a/t - not determinable). Then
  clearly "a", "r", then minims. The minim group after "r" is three or four
  strokes: readable as "ni", "ui", "m", or "in"; a faint hairline over the
  last strokes may be an i-stroke or an abbreviation mark, uncertain because a
  metal pin/nail head and abrasion sit exactly there. So the group is
  "-arni" / "-arui" / "-arm" / "-arin", with "-tarni"/"-tarui" as my best
  guess for the whole (?). After a word space: a tall letter with a foot
  followed by a short stroke: "si" (long s + i) most likely, "fi" or "li"
  possible. Nothing further survives to the right.
line 2 (staff): red staff lines (three visible in this tile, a fourth at the
        fold at the bottom). Black notation: one large compound sign made of
        lozenge heads joined to a vertical stem (two or three lozenges stacked
        diagonally with a descending stem), and to its right a single detached
        lozenge (punctum) sitting on the second visible line. At the lower
        left, below the bottom staff line and partly in the fold, two more
        black lozenge/square note heads are visible. No text under this staff
        is in frame.

image-003.jpg
line 1 (same strip, left part; mostly under the pastedown): a large red
        initial, lower half only visible - a broad letter with a crossbar and
        two feet, best read as "A" (?); its top is covered by paper. To its
        left, two thin red vertical rules (frame/margin rules) and a small red
        flourish or hook crossing them. To the right of the initial, on the
        staff: red staff lines (three visible) and one black sign shaped like
        a bowl with a thin upward tail - either a note/clef form or the lower
        part of a black letter (c- or e-like bowl); I cannot decide which.
        Above and left of it, a small black mark at the tear (fragment of
        another sign). No readable text in this tile beyond the initial.
line 2 (bottom edge, in the fold): tips of two black lozenge note heads and a
        further red line, i.e. the continuation of the staff or the next one.

SEPARATE ITEM (not manuscript text of the fragment)
image-001.jpg, label on pastedown, handwritten, sideways: 3546

LIMITATIONS
- Only one partial text line of the parchment waste is exposed; its beginning
  is under the pastedown and its end is cut by the strip edge. Roughly one
  word-ending and one two-letter word survive. This is far too little for a
  connected reading; no span of several lines exists in these images.
- The minim group in image-002 line 1 is ambiguous as stated, and is partly
  obscured by a nail head.
- Whether the black bowl-shaped sign in image-003 is notation or lettering is
  undetermined.
- The facing leaf (cursive script with red) is visible only as an upside-down
  sliver and was not read. A view of that leaf, and any lifting or imaging
  under the pastedown, would be needed for more text.
